text:
Under their red spines, in the dark mahogany,

Your books sleep. I follow the latest authors:

Other forms attract me, other new colors

And the current steals me toward your pagan feasts.


I enjoy fierce styles — wide wolf teeth.

Others sober, meticulous — watchful cypresses.

Others white and fine — columns beneath flowers.

Others acidic and ocher — bedroom storms.


I had already forgotten you and by chance I take you up again,

And at the first verses there rises from the volume

Your fresh and fine breath of fragrant honeys.


Lover to whom one returns as the first time:

You are the sweet mouth that back there, in spring,

Liquefied in our veins an entire forest of roses.

translation.title: Under Their Red Backs, in the Dark Mahogany...
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem as a reading encounter that becomes erotic return.
